guideTitle: Platinum in Leonida — GTA VI Trophy Guide
intro: This is a working guide, not a trophy list with hints stapled to it. Every card below starts from the official wording of its trophy, explains what that wording commits you to, and then gives you a method: the order to do things in, the preparation that makes the attempt cheap, and the point at which an attempt has failed and should be restarted. Work the roadmap from the top. The story comes first because it unlocks the map, the contacts and the income everything else depends on; the long counts come last because the story and the sweeps feed them for free while you play.
honestyNote: A note on what this guide does not know. Every trophy name, description, grade and tracked count here is taken from the official PlayStation 5 list. This edition was revised on 20 November 2026, the day after launch, against two post-launch trophy guides — PowerPyx and GTABase — and most of the triggers that were unconfirmed before launch are now described in public, so the cards that use them say so and name the source. Three grades of knowledge remain, and each card tells you which one it is: facts both post-launch guides agree on; methods reported by PowerPyx alone, where GTABase still lists the trophy as unconfirmed — those cards name PowerPyx in the text and say the other guide has not confirmed it; and one trophy, Bad Luck, I Guess, whose trigger both guides still list as unknown, which keeps its watch flag and its save-first method. Where a card's method is this guide's own, it says that too.
sourcesNote: Sources used across the guide: the official PlayStation 5 trophy list for Grand Theft Auto VI (names, descriptions, grades and tracked counts), as carried in this kit's starter data and as listed publicly by Exophase and PSNProfiles, the two listings the bounty rules name and which agree on every name, description and grade; and, for the post-launch revision of 20 November 2026, the trophy guides of PowerPyx and GTABase, checked that day, for unlock windows, trigger details and missable status. Each card repeats its own source line so the card stands on its own when printed or shared.

roadmap.title: Story first, with rotating saves
roadmap.text: Play the campaign straight through: the chapter trophies and the named-mission trophies all pay out along the way, and finishing unlocks the contacts, activities and earning methods the rest of the list needs. Keep three manual save slots and rotate them before every chapter ending and every big set-piece. That habit matters more than it did before launch, because the post-launch guides (PowerPyx and GTABase, checked 20 November 2026) confirm there is no mission replay in this game: your saves are the only way back to any story moment. One story-adjacent job inside this stop cannot wait for later at all — the Chapter 1 meditation on the Positive Mental Attitude card, the one possibly missable item on the list.
roadmap.trophies: Just Like Paradise, Paradise Lost, T**s Ass Drug Money, Vice City, Baby!, Top Of The World, Ma, You Gotta Know When to Get Off, Trust, Break the Bank, Family Matters, DWNFALL, Hi-Jacked, Snow Storm

roadmap.title: Close out every contact
roadmap.text: With the story done, work the named contacts one at a time and finish each person's whole strand before starting the next. Five contacts each end in a final-mission trophy and Bret's strand ends in a hunt — but plan the silver Strangers & Freaks separately: the post-launch guides (PowerPyx and GTABase, checked 20 November 2026) report that the named contacts' questlines do not count toward it, and name the strands that do. The Strangers & Freaks card carries the confirmed list; this stop is for the bronzes, each earned for itself. Strands are easy to lose track of when you interleave them, so do one person per session and tick the card the moment their last mission ends.
roadmap.trophies: Road to Rehabilitation, This Was No Boat Accident, The Lone Rider, Supply & Demand, Spin On This!, Fair Game, Strangers & Freaks

roadmap.title: Sample everything once, then get good at it
roadmap.text: Try every activity type a single time to bank Master of None, then settle into the skill work: shooting-range golds, drone races, race wins, the fishing duel, the arcade, and challenges in batches. None of these can be missed, so a failed run is just tuition — change exactly one thing between attempts (vehicle, weapon, line, time of day) and go again while the course is still in your hands.
roadmap.trophies: Master of None, The Shootist, Top Fun, Earn Cash, Not Kudos, Baited My Tackle, Stick Fiddler, One Last Thing

roadmap.title: Sweep the map region by region
roadmap.text: Clear Leonida one region at a time instead of chasing single items across the state. Meditation spots, card sets, WAiNK locations and unvisited areas all sit in the same neighbourhoods, so one planned pass per region collects four lists at once. Scan whatever vehicles you pass with the WAiNK app rather than driving them — discovery in this game is a scan, per the Whip It Good card — and the 100-vehicle count fills itself in as a side effect.
roadmap.trophies: Positive Mental Attitude, Don't Touch My Deck, You WAiNKer!, The Goodtime State, Whip It Good

roadmap.title: Crime with your partner, money with a plan
roadmap.text: Do the crime set now, while your balance and map knowledge are at their peak: the stealth jewellery job first, planned properly, because it fails on being seen rather than on firepower; then vaults, the armoured truck and one illegal operation per gang. The two partner trophies need a wanted level raised and managed on purpose, so pick ground whose exits you already know. Money trophies are bookkeeping, not events: launder marked bills whenever you are holding them, let shop spending accumulate naturally, register vehicles as you steal them, and buy the garages last, when story income has topped out.
roadmap.trophies: Hot Together, Retail Therapy, Sneakthief, Maximum Withdrawal, A Classic Blitz Play, Pest Control, Dime on the Dollar, Treat Yo Self, Little Boxes, On the Spot

roadmap.title: Feats, strange moments, and the last percent
roadmap.text: What remains is a mixed bag: combat feats you can set up deliberately, the strange-moment trophies — most of them with confirmed, card-level recipes since the post-launch revision, and one, Bad Luck, I Guess, still honestly unknown — the stunt total you have been feeding since the story, and the 100% completion push that sweeps up whatever the earlier stops left behind. The platinum pays itself the moment the fifty-fourth other trophy lands, so if you reach this stop with only A Long Road outstanding, you are one checklist audit away from finishing.
roadmap.trophies: Gunslinger, Challenging Tank, Ten Pin, Catch Me If You Can, In The Beginning…, Capital Offense, Let’s Go Bowling, Personal Best, Actions Speak Louder, Bad Luck, I Guess, The Truth Is Out There, Cunning Stunts, A Long Road, Vice Got a Price!

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum asks for nothing of its own: it unlocks the moment the other fifty-four trophies on this list are all earned. There is no separate task to prepare for, so the only strategy is sequencing — use the roadmap above so that no long count is left as a lone grind at the end, and check this card whenever you want a single number for how close you are: it is earned minus one.
steps: Earn trophies in roadmap order so unlocks and income arrive before the trophies that need them.
Audit the checklist after each roadmap stop and clear stragglers while their areas are still familiar.
When one trophy remains, this one follows it automatically.
trophies.tip: If a single trophy is blocking the platinum, it is almost always a count you stopped feeding early — restart the habit, not the game.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: The official requirement is a single named mission: Gone Fishing, the game's opening job. Play through it and the trophy lands at the mission's end — there is no performance condition attached, no medal or time target in the wording. Treat this mission as your controls tutorial as well as your first trophy: the driving, shooting and wanted-level basics it teaches are the exact skills the skill trophies later in the list are built on.
steps: Start a new game and follow the opening mission markers.
Complete Gone Fishing at any pace and on any approach.
The trophy unlocks as the mission wraps up.
trophies.tip: Do not rush the opener — an extra ten minutes learning the wanted system here saves hours on the partner crime trophies later.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: A chapter-completion trophy: finish Chapter 1 and this pays out — with one timing quirk worth knowing before you start. PowerPyx's post-launch trophy guide reports that the trophy does not pop at the chapter break itself but after you complete the first main mission of Chapter 2, What's in the Bag?; GTABase's trophy list reports the same delayed unlock. So do not panic, and do not reload, if the credits for Chapter 1 roll without a bronze. Chapter 1 is also where this guide's two protective habits begin, and both are cheaper to start here than to retrofit: keep a manual save from before the chapter's closing missions until this trophy has actually landed, and, before you leave Chapter 1 behind, take the Chapter 1 meditation moment flagged on the Positive Mental Attitude card — PowerPyx and GTABase both identify it as the one possibly missable item on the whole list.
steps: Play Chapter 1's missions in the order the game offers them, and take the Chapter 1 meditation moment described on the Positive Mental Attitude card before finishing the chapter.
Before the chapter's closing missions, save manually in a fresh slot and do not overwrite that slot yet.
Finish Chapter 1, then keep playing into Chapter 2 and complete its first main mission, What's in the Bag? — the trophy is reported to unlock at that point.
Once it lands, tick it here and audit your early counts (vehicles discovered, WAiNK scans) while the areas are still familiar.
trophies.tip: A delayed pop is not a missed trophy: for this one, judge it only after Chapter 2's first mission is done — reloading a Chapter 1 save before that point throws away the very mission that triggers it.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Delayed-unlock timing and the Chapter 1 meditation warning: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Chapter 2's completion trophy, earned by playing the chapter to its end. The name is censored on PlayStation itself — that spelling is the official one, not a typo in this guide. As with Chapter 1 there is no extra condition in the wording. By this point the map and the contact system are opening up; resist the urge to wander off for collectibles yet, because story progress keeps paying out the unlocks the sweep stops depend on.
steps: Complete Chapter 2's mission chain in order.
Keep rotating a manual save before each mission finale.
The trophy unlocks when the chapter closes.
trophies.tip: If a side activity catches your eye during Chapter 2, note its location and keep moving — the roadmap comes back for all of them in one pass.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3 to earn this one — and, as with Chapter 1's trophy, expect the pop to lag the chapter break. PowerPyx's post-launch trophy guide reports that this bronze unlocks only after you complete the first two main missions of Chapter 4, Ocean Beach and Another Life; GTABase's trophy list reports the same timing. Treat those two missions as part of this trophy's requirement in practice: keep playing, and only audit this card once both are done. Chapter 3 is also the hinge of the whole run, because several systems the later stops depend on open inside it, on the sources named below: the Key Cloner arrives in a Chapter 3 mission, Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs run in Chapter 3, and Randy's and Tyrone's strands both get marked from Chapter 3 missions. None of that has to be finished inside the chapter — all of it remains available after the story — but noticing each unlock as it happens is what turns the post-story clean-up from a scavenger hunt into a checklist.
steps: Play Chapter 3's missions in order, keeping a manual save from before the chapter's closing missions until this trophy lands.

As Chapter 3 systems open — the Key Cloner mission, Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs, and the first markers for Randy's and Tyrone's strands — note each one; you will come back to all of them in the contact and crime stops.
Continue into Chapter 4 and complete its first two main missions, Ocean Beach and Another Life; the trophy is reported to unlock at that point.
Audit before moving on: if the bronze is still missing after both missions, check this card against your mission log the same day, while a reload is still cheap.
trophies.tip: Judge this trophy two missions late, not at the chapter break — and use the wait productively: those first two Chapter 4 missions are story time you had to play anyway, so the delay costs nothing if you expect it.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Delayed-unlock timing and Chapter 3 unlocks: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Chapter 4's completion trophy. Same shape as the earlier chapters: the official text asks only that you finish the chapter. What changes by now is the stakes of your save discipline — the endgame is close enough that a one-off moment missed here is expensive to return to if mission replay turns out to be limited, so keep the three-slot rotation going and never overwrite the save from before a chapter finale until the next chapter is underway.
steps: Complete Chapter 4's missions in sequence.
Save before the finale and keep that slot untouched until the next chapter is rolling.
The trophy unlocks as the chapter ends.
trophies.tip: Give your save slots a pattern — before finale, after finale, free roam — so you can always tell which one is safe to overwrite.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The gold for finishing the campaign's final mission — and this card has come off the watch list, because the two facts it was waiting on are now confirmed in public. PowerPyx's post-launch trophy guide states that there is still free-roam after the story but no mission replay, and lists this trophy as an automatic story trophy that cannot be missed; GTABase's trophy list says the same and adds that no trophy depends on how you play a mission. So the ending is not a lock-out: finish the story, and the whole map, every contact strand and every clean-up trophy remain available to you afterwards. What the absence of mission replay does change is your save discipline, not your route: because no story mission can be replayed, the manual saves you kept at chapter starts and ends are the only way back to any story moment, which is why this guide keeps recommending them even though no trophy here is missable.
steps: Before starting the final mission, make a dedicated manual save and label the slot as your pre-finale save; do not overwrite it afterwards.
Complete the final mission; the gold unlocks at its conclusion.
After the credits, confirm you are back in free-roam, then work the clean-up stops from this save — every remaining trophy on this list is still reachable from here, per the sources below.
Keep the pre-finale save for the whole clean-up: with no mission replay, it is your only route back to story-only moments.
trophies.tip: The point of no return in this game is a save-slot problem, not a trophy problem: one untouched pre-finale save gives you everything a replay function would, for every trophy on this list.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Free-roam after the story, no mission replay, and cannot-be-missed status: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the named story mission Breakfast Run, a Chapter 2 main mission — both PowerPyx's and GTABase's post-launch guides place it there and class it as an automatic story trophy that cannot be missed. Placement matters more than the mission itself, because Chapter 2 is the chapter where this list quietly starts its long counts: the same chapter's Coffee Break mission is the one that unlocks free-roaming together as both characters (see Hot Together and Personal Best), and the Scooter Bros app and the purchasable garages also arrive through Chapter 2 missions, per the sources below. So use Breakfast Run as a dated checkpoint rather than a task: when it pops, you are in the chapter where partnering up, vehicle registration and garage buying all switch on, and the habits on those cards should start from here, not from the endgame.
steps: Before starting Breakfast Run, save manually in a fresh slot — Chapter 2 is worth a clean entry point, because several unlocks land inside it.
Complete Breakfast Run as the story presents it; the trophy unlocks during the mission's completion, with no extra condition.
Tick the card immediately, then check which Chapter 2 unlocks you now hold (partner free-roam after Coffee Break, the Scooter Bros app, garage purchases) and start the habits on those cards.

If the bronze has not appeared by the mission-complete screen, reload the pre-mission save and replay it the same session — with no mission replay in this game, a same-day reload is the only fix there will ever be.
trophies.tip: Treat this card as a calendar, not a chore: its real content is 'you are now in Chapter 2', and Chapter 2 is where the partner, registration and garage systems all switch on.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Chapter 2 placement, cannot-be-missed status and the chapter's unlocks: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission The Cartel Heist, a Chapter 3 main mission — PowerPyx and GTABase both place it there and class it as an automatic story trophy that cannot be missed. Read it as the campaign's rehearsal for the crime stop, and rehearse specific things, not just a mood: how the mission stages its entry, how long it lets you work before the response arrives, and how its getaway is routed. Those three timings are the whole skill set of the free-roam robbery trophies, and the post-launch sources below put numbers on the later version of the same job: large bank vault robberies, unlocked in Chapter 4, always give a four-star wanted level and pay up to $205,000 each. A player who watched how The Cartel Heist handles its four-star escape already knows the shape of the vault routine; a player who rushed it has to learn that shape later, at full price, in free roam.
steps: Before starting The Cartel Heist, save manually in a fresh slot, and go in with full health and your best current vehicle staged as the mission allows.
Play the heist slowly enough to register its structure: note the entry method, the moment the wanted level arrives, and the route the escape takes.
Complete the heist including its escape; the trophy unlocks during the mission's completion, with no performance condition.

Afterwards, write down the one escape habit the mission taught you — breaking line of sight before changing vehicles, or the reverse — and tick the card; that habit is your default plan for Maximum Withdrawal and Hot Together later.
trophies.tip: Your getaway note from this mission should be one sentence you could act on half-asleep — 'lose sight first, swap cars second' or its opposite. If you cannot write it, you watched a cutscene, not a rehearsal.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Chapter 3 placement and cannot-be-missed status, and the bank-vault figures used for comparison: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play, a Chapter 4 main mission — PowerPyx and GTABase both place it there and class it as an automatic story trophy that cannot be missed. That confirmation changes how you should treat the mission's personal moments. Earlier versions of this card warned that a conversation or choice inside it might secretly carry a trophy; the post-launch sources below remove that worry: GTABase states plainly that no trophy depends on how you play a mission, and PowerPyx's roadmap lists exactly one possibly missable trophy on the whole list, which is not this one. So play Child's Play for the story, take optional interactions because they are there rather than out of fear, and spend the attention you save on the thing Chapter 4 actually unlocks for the trophy run: the optional mission That's Where The Money Is…, which both sources name as the gateway to large bank vault robberies, and with them the Maximum Withdrawal, A Classic Blitz Play and Hot Together trophies.
steps: Before starting Child's Play, save manually in a fresh slot — Chapter 4 is dense with unlocks, and a clean entry point is worth one slot.
Complete Child's Play as the story presents it; the trophy unlocks during the mission's completion, with no condition on choices or performance.
Tick the card, then check whether the Chapter 4 optional mission That's Where The Money Is… is now marked on your map — that marker, not this bronze, is the chapter's real prize for the crime stop.
If the bronze did not appear at completion, reload the pre-mission save and replay it the same day; there is no mission replay later.
trophies.tip: Spend fear where the sources say it belongs — one Chapter 1 meditation — and spend none here: a confirmed unmissable mission trophy is a place to enjoy the story with your guard down.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Chapter 4 placement, cannot-be-missed status and the bank-vault gateway mission: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Headliners, a Chapter 4 main mission — PowerPyx and GTABase both place it there and class it as an automatic story trophy that cannot be missed. This card's old text suggested using the named-mission trophies to confirm that a story replay is registering progress; that advice is withdrawn, because the post-launch sources below confirm there is no mission replay in this game at all. The checkpoint idea survives in a sharper form: precisely because a missed registration can never be repaired by replaying, the audit has to happen at the only moment it can — immediately. When Headliners ends, stop for ten seconds and confirm three things before you play another mission: the bronze appeared, this card is ticked, and your rotating save from before the mission is still untouched. That ten-second habit, applied to every named-mission trophy, is the entire defence against the one failure mode this game's structure cannot forgive.
steps: Before starting Headliners, save manually in a fresh slot and leave that slot untouched until the trophy is confirmed.
Complete Headliners as the story presents it; the trophy unlocks during the mission's completion, with no extra condition.
At the mission-complete screen, verify the pop before doing anything else: bronze seen, card ticked here, pre-mission save still intact.
If any of the three checks fails, reload the pre-mission save and replay the mission now — later there is no replay option to fall back on.
trophies.tip: In a game with no mission replay, 'check it popped' is not bookkeeping, it is the whole strategy — ten seconds at the completion screen replaces a feature the game does not have.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Chapter 4 placement, cannot-be-missed status and the absence of mission replay: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown. VCIA is the airport, and this mission is worth your attention beyond its own trophy: the airport is also the setting of the Catch Me If You Can curiosity trophy further down the list, so the layout, vehicle placement and escape routes you learn here are the raw material for that attempt later. Finish the mission for the bronze, and file the geography away.
steps: Reach VCIA Takedown in the story sequence.
Complete the mission, noting the airport's roads and exits as you go.
The trophy unlocks when the mission completes.
trophies.tip: Story missions double as reconnaissance — anywhere a mission takes you is somewhere a later trophy probably wants you to perform.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The requirement is completion, plainly worded; the card is spoiler-shielded because the mission sits in Chapter 5, the final chapter, and even discussing its setting gives story away — that placement, and its status as an automatic story trophy that cannot be missed, are the two facts the post-launch sources below confirm, and they are all this card will say about the mission itself. What can be said without spoilers is procedural, and it matters more here than anywhere else in the story: this is the last named-mission trophy before the finale, so it is the final chance to practise the endgame routine — a dedicated manual save before the mission, a confirmed pop at its end, and a checklist audit while the campaign's shape is still fresh. Do that audit properly and the finale becomes a formality: every story bronze ticked, the pre-finale save habit already automatic, and nothing left in the story column to wonder about.
steps: Before starting Operation Savage Glory, save manually in a fresh slot — your last story save before the finale routine begins.
Complete the mission as the story presents it; the trophy unlocks at completion, with no extra condition.
Confirm the pop at the completion screen, tick the card, and then audit the whole story set: every chapter trophy and named-mission bronze should now be ticked except the finale's gold.
Keep both this save and a new pre-finale save untouched from here on; with no mission replay, they are your only way back into the late campaign.
trophies.tip: The shield hides this card's subject, not its procedure: save first, confirm the pop, audit the set — a routine you can follow without reading a single spoiler.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Chapter 5 placement and cannot-be-missed status: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The second gold, and the list's true final exam: reach 100% on the game's own completion counter. The official wording does not enumerate what the counter includes, so work from the game's completion screen rather than from this trophy list — the two are related but not identical, and the counter is the authority. Almost everything in the roadmap feeds it. When you stall in the high nineties, the missing fraction is usually a category you sampled once for Master of None and never finished, so audit category by category instead of wandering.
steps: Finish the story, all contact strands and all activity types first — they carry most of the counter.
Open the in-game completion screen and list every category that is not yet full.
Clear the remaining categories one at a time, re-checking the counter after each.
trophies.tip: Chase the counter, not the trophy: screenshot your completion screen at 90% and work only from what it says is missing.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. The completion counter's contents are read from the game itself; method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Two hundred and fifty completed stunts — the biggest single count on the list, and a silver for a reason. The number comes straight from the official description, and the only sane way to reach it is to start early and never do a dedicated stunt session until the end: hit stunts opportunistically whenever travel puts one in front of you, because stunt opportunities sit along the same roads the story and the sweeps use. Whatever remains after the roadmap's fifth stop gets finished in focused loops on the stunt-densest ground you found along the way.
steps: Take every stunt opportunity that appears during story and sweep travel; do not drive past one.
Note the areas where stunts cluster while you explore — those become your finishing loops.
Grind the remainder in those loops, checking the tracked count every twenty or so completions.
trophies.tip: Repeating a stunt you have already mastered is faster than hunting new ones — for a count this size, boring and reliable beats scenic.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade and the tracked count of 250), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every activity type the game offers, once each — the starter data puts the number of types at nine. Trying is the whole requirement: you do not need to win, medal or finish well, just start each type properly once. Do this early in the activities stop, because the sampling tour is also your scouting run: it shows you which activities you are naturally good at, which is where your gold-medal and race-win efforts should concentrate afterwards.
steps: Open the activities list and note every distinct type on offer.
Start each type once and play it far enough to register as tried.
The trophy unlocks when the last untried type has been sampled.
trophies.tip: Keep a note of your first-attempt results per type — the ones you nearly won cold are your cheapest golds later.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; the count of activity types comes from the kit's starter data for this list. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold in every Shooting Range challenge — forty-two of them, per the starter data. This is a consistency trophy, not a talent trophy: gold thresholds reward accuracy routines, not heroics. Work one weapon class at a time, learn where targets appear rather than reacting to them, and treat your first run on any layout as reconnaissance for the scoring run that follows. If a challenge resists, change the weapon before you change your expectations — the right tool usually moves a silver to a gold on its own.
steps: Run each challenge once to learn its target pattern, without chasing the medal.
Replay immediately with the weapon that best fits the layout, aiming for clean streaks over speed.
Move on the moment a gold lands; save stubborn layouts for a fresh session.
trophies.tip: Accuracy streaks are the currency here — a slower run with no misses beats a fast run with resprays on almost every layout.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; the count of 42 challenges comes from the kit's starter data for this list. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location — fourteen locations, per the starter data. A win at each site is required, not participation, so expect to learn each course: fly it once slowly to find the racing line and the gates that punish greed, then attack it. Drone handling rewards smoothness over throttle; the pilots who win these are the ones who stop crashing, not the ones who fly fastest between crashes.
steps: Fly each location once at cruising speed to learn the gate order and the tight corners.
Race it properly, prioritising a clean line over raw pace.
Tick the location off only on a win, and move to the next site.
trophies.tip: If one course keeps beating you, watch where you lose time rather than where you crash — slow gates, not walls, are usually the problem.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; the count of 14 locations comes from the kit's starter data for this list. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win twenty different races — different is the operative word in the official text, so repeating your favourite circuit twenty times earns you one unit of progress, not twenty. Spread your wins across the race calendar, starting with the shortest and slowest classes where fields are forgiving, and learn the two skills that decide most races in this series: a clean first corner, and defending your line rather than chasing the car ahead into its mistakes.
steps: List the races available to you and start with the shortest events.
Win each race once; a win only counts toward the twenty if the race is a new one.
Work up to longer events as your vehicle options and course knowledge grow.
trophies.tip: Twenty different wins is a breadth test — keep a written list, because the game will happily let you re-win a race you already banked.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade and the count of 20), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal — a named character — in a fishing challenge. The official wording makes this a duel, not a solo target: you need the challenge against Cal specifically, and you need to win it. Fishing mechanics in this series reward patience and timing over reflexes, so learn the cast-and-reel rhythm on ordinary fishing first, where losing costs nothing, and only then take Cal on. If the challenge can be retried — the usual pattern for activities — treat the first attempt as a scouting run for his scoring pace.
steps: Practise ordinary fishing until casting and reeling feel automatic.
Start Cal's fishing challenge and watch what score or catch he posts.
Beat his result; if the attempt fails, retry with the rhythm you have just measured.
trophies.tip: Duels are won on consistency — a steady run of decent catches beats one heroic fish and a string of lost ones.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Challenge format details beyond the official wording are this guide's own method, not confirmed specifics.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — one, not all of them, and complete rather than merely play: the post-launch sources below define completion as finishing all of a game's levels at least once, with no need to beat its challenges. You may not even need to leave home to do it. PowerPyx's and GTABase's guides agree there are four video games in total — Tenebrae Lux, Street Trash III and Time Jackers Rewind, playable at the TV at home by interacting with the controllers and available already during Chapter 1, plus Bang For Your Buck on arcade cabinets around Leonida. Pick whichever of the three home games suits you, play it at home during a quiet story gap, and the lightest bronze on the list is banked before most players have found an arcade. Note the availability caveat both sources imply: during some story sections the home TV is temporarily unavailable, but the games return afterwards and remain available after the story.
steps: At home, interact with the controllers by the TV and choose one of the three home games: Tenebrae Lux, Street Trash III or Time Jackers Rewind.
Play that one game through all of its levels at least once — finishing the levels is the requirement; its side challenges are not.
The trophy unlocks when the game ends in completion; tick the card and count the session toward the arcade/video-game type in your Master of None sampling.
Fallback: if the home TV is unavailable during your current story section, use a Bang For Your Buck cabinet in the world instead, or simply wait — the home games are still there after the story.
trophies.tip: Do not go hunting for an arcade for this one — the shortest route to the trophy is your own living-room TV in Chapter 1, and the cabinet game is the backup, not the plan.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. The four games, the home-TV route and the definition of completion: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's strand: work through every mission Andy gives you until the final one, and complete that. Stranger strands unlock in sequence, so if Andy has gone quiet, the next step is usually gated behind story progress, time passing in-game, or a phone call you have not waited for yet — keep playing other content and check back rather than camping on his marker. The trophy pays on the final mission only, which is why this guide insists on finishing strands in one sitting once they open up.
steps: Take every mission Andy offers, in order, as they appear.
If the strand stalls, advance the story or let in-game time pass, then return.
Complete Andy's final mission; the trophy unlocks at its end.
trophies.tip: A strand that will not advance is almost never bugged — it is waiting on a trigger. Change location, sleep, or finish a story mission and come back.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's final mission — and now the strand has a concrete shape, because both post-launch sources below describe the same job. Kenton, marked with a green KR icon in Key Lento, hires you to recover treasure from seven shipwrecks: he marks purple chest icons on the map, you dive at those markers and use the metal detector to dig the treasure up, and you bring it back to him. Progress is tracked in the game under Progress > Collections > Kenton's Treasures, so the strand is never a memory test. The one behaviour that used to make players abandon this card is also explained by the sources: after Chapter 1 Kenton disappears for a while, then texts Jason again later in the game — GTABase says plainly that you can finish it then, and PowerPyx adds that all of his quests remain available after the story. A silent Kenton is a paused strand, not a failed one. One correction this card also owes you: despite being a stranger strand in everyday language, Kenton's line is not one of the strands the Strangers & Freaks silver is confirmed to count — see that card before you plan around it.
steps: Start the strand when Kenton's green KR marker appears in Key Lento during Chapter 1, and work the shipwrecks he marks in purple.
At each wreck, dive at the chest marker and sweep with the metal detector until the treasure is dug up, then return it to Kenton.
Check Progress > Collections > Kenton's Treasures after each delivery so your count of the seven wrecks is the game's, not your memory's.

If Kenton goes quiet after Chapter 1, do not camp on his shop: play other content until his text arrives later in the game, then finish the remaining wrecks — the strand is still completable after the story.
Complete the seventh wreck and his final mission; the trophy unlocks at completion.
trophies.tip: Track wrecks, not sessions: 'four of seven, and he owes me a text' is a state you can act on next week; 'somewhere in Kenton's strand' is not.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Seven shipwrecks, the Key Lento marker, the tracking menu and Kenton's Chapter 1 disappearance and return: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's strand by completing his final mission — a chain of five jobs, and both post-launch sources below name them and the place they start. Billy's questline is marked automatically at the Thrillbilly Mudclub in Kelly County after the Chapter 2 main mission Coffee Break, and its five jobs run: Thrillbillies, Twist Wrist, Smash, Grab, Mall Rats, The Impaler, and finally Hometown Heroes, which awards the trophy. All five remain available after the story, so a paused Billy is never an emergency. This card also carries a correction to its own earlier advice: it used to tell you to count Billy toward your eight finished strands for Strangers & Freaks, and that was wrong. PowerPyx and GTABase both report that Billy's questline does not count toward that silver — the confirmed counting strands are other people's. Earn this bronze for itself, and plan the silver from the Strangers & Freaks card's confirmed list instead.
steps: After Chapter 2's Coffee Break, go to the Thrillbilly Mudclub in Kelly County where Billy's strand is marked.
Work the five jobs in order — Thrillbillies; Twist Wrist, Smash, Grab; Mall Rats; The Impaler; Hometown Heroes — ticking each one off as it closes.
Complete Hometown Heroes; the trophy unlocks at its end.
Do not add Billy to your Strangers & Freaks tally: per the sources below, this strand does not count toward the silver.
trophies.tip: Five named jobs beat one vague strand: if you cannot name the next Billy job on the list above, you are not stuck, you are between jobs — check the Mudclub marker.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Start point, the five job names, post-story availability and the Strangers & Freaks exclusion: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: The silver for finishing eight whole stranger strands anywhere in Leonida — and this card has been rewritten because its earlier version was wrong in a way that would have wasted your hours. It claimed the six named contact strands on this list (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and Bret) gave you six of the eight. The post-launch sources below report the opposite: the game does not count those questlines as Strangers & Freaks at all. PowerPyx names the strands confirmed to count — Kirk, Kyle, Yago and Pilot Pete, with more still being discovered — and lists Moses, Tyrone, Yasmani, Andy, Billy and Eddie among those that do not count; GTABase's list agrees on both the counting four and the exclusions. So plan the silver around the confirmed four, use the trophy's own progress tracker in your PlayStation trophy list as the authority for every further strand, and treat the named contacts' cards as what they are: separate bronzes worth earning, which simply do not pay into this silver. All of these strands remain available after the story, per both sources.
steps: Finish the confirmed counting strands first: Kirk, Kyle, Yago and Pilot Pete, completing each person's full chain, not just their opener.
After each finished strand, check the trophy's progress tracker in your PlayStation trophy list and record the new count here — the tracker, not this card, is the authority on what counted.
For the remaining strands, work other stranger markers you find in the world, and keep only the ones the tracker credits; expect the confirmed list to grow as the sources below update theirs.
Do not budget Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone, Bret, Moses, Yasmani or Eddie toward this silver — per the sources below, their strands do not count.
The silver unlocks when the tracker reaches eight credited strands.
trophies.tip: A stuck count at four is not a bug and not half-finished strands — it is the confirmed list running out. Check the tracker, then hunt new stranger markers instead of polishing contacts that never counted.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade and the count of 8), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Which strands count (Kirk, Kyle, Yago, Pilot Pete) and which do not: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's final mission to close his strand — which is not a chain of errands but a shopping list. Both post-launch sources below describe the same structure: Randy's Wish List opens after the Chapter 3 mission Clonin' Keys, Makin' GS, the mission that gives you the Key Cloner and has you deliver a sports car to Randy as part of the story. From there he wants sixteen named sports cars in total. He is marked with a green RK icon in the west of Vice City, the list itself is tracked under Map > Robberies > Randy's Wish List, and he marks some cars for you in fixed locations while others you simply find. The working method the sources support: scan high-end sports cars with the WAiNK app to see whether one is on his list — when you enter or scan a wanted car, the game prompts you to deliver it — and drive it to his garage intact, because both sources note that cars delivered in good condition pay more. GTABase adds the best hunting ground: hotel driveways around Vice Beach and Ocean Beach. The whole list can still be completed after the story. And one correction carried over from the silver's card: Randy's strand, like the other named contacts, does not count toward Strangers & Freaks.
steps: Unlock the strand by playing Chapter 3's Clonin' Keys, Makin' GS, which gives you the Key Cloner and your first delivery to Randy.
Open Map > Robberies > Randy's Wish List and work from the game's list of sixteen cars, not from memory.

Hunt where the sources point: the cars Randy marks in fixed locations first, then hotel driveways around Vice Beach and Ocean Beach, scanning candidates with the WAiNK app (hold Up on the D-pad, then R1) to check them against the list.
Deliver each wanted car to Randy's garage (green RK icon, west Vice City) in good condition — a careful drive pays more than a fast one.
The trophy unlocks when the list is complete and his final mission closes; do not count this strand toward Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.tip: Sixteen named cars is a checklist, not a vibe: if a sports car is not on the Wish List screen, it is traffic, however expensive it looks — scan first, steal second.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Wish List structure, sixteen cars, Key Cloner unlock, tracking menu, hunting grounds and condition-based pay: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's strand with its final mission — a two-quest demolition job, not a long chain, and both post-launch sources below lay out the same sequence. Tyrone's questline is marked automatically after the Chapter 3 main mission Here, Kitty Kitty, and it is available only while playing as Jason. Purple map markers then show Synthetic Labs around Vice City: the first quest, Take Out Kitty Litter, has you destroying those labs, and once enough of them are gone Tyrone gives the second quest, Spin On This (Shut Down the Labs), which unlocks the trophy on completion. The whole strand remains available after the story. Two planning notes follow from the sources. First, character matters: if you arrive as Lucia, the strand will look absent when it is merely waiting for Jason. Second, the correction from the silver's card applies here too — Tyrone's strand is one of the questlines both sources explicitly list as not counting toward Strangers & Freaks, so tick this bronze for itself and keep your silver tally on the confirmed strands only.
steps: Finish Chapter 3's Here, Kitty Kitty as part of the story, then switch to Jason — Tyrone's strand does not run for Lucia.
Follow the purple Synthetic Lab markers around Vice City and destroy labs for Take Out Kitty Litter, checking the markers off as each lab falls.
When Tyrone offers Spin On This (Shut Down the Labs), take it and shut down the remaining labs it names.
Complete that second quest; the trophy unlocks at its completion, and the strand can still be finished after the story if you left it.
Do not add Tyrone to your Strangers & Freaks tally: per the sources below, this strand does not count toward the silver.
trophies.tip: If Tyrone's markers are missing, check your character before you check the map — a Jason-only strand viewed as Lucia looks exactly like a bug and is neither.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Unlock point, Jason-only availability, the two quests and the Strangers & Freaks exclusion: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot in Leonida — eighteen spots, per the starter data — and this card now carries the watch flag, because both post-launch sources below identify it as the one possibly missable trophy on the entire list. The risk is a single Chapter 1 moment: PowerPyx reports that at some point in Chapter 1, in the morning after the mission Down to Earth, Lucia talks about meditating in the kitchen at Jason's house and walks out to the balcony; follow her, talk to her there and choose Accept, and she teaches you to meditate. That session raises the meditation counter by one but is not marked as a Meditation Spot like the others, it becomes permanently unavailable after Chapter 1, and — PowerPyx is explicit about this — it is still unconfirmed whether the trophy actually requires it; GTABase flags the same moment as possibly missable on the same reasoning. The honest summary: the other spots are a pure sweep, this one is a cheap insurance policy. Take the two minutes in Chapter 1 and the question never matters. For the sweep itself, both sources add the mechanics that make it tractable: meditating at a spot with both Jason and Lucia counts twice at the same location, progress is tracked under Progress > Collections > Exploration > Meditations, and the final spot cannot be done until playing both characters together unlocks in Chapter 2.
steps: In Chapter 1, the morning after Down to Earth, talk to Lucia in the kitchen at Jason's house, follow her to the balcony when she goes to meditate, and choose Accept — before you finish Chapter 1, because the moment does not come back.
From then on, fold the remaining spots into the region-by-region sweep, meditating with both characters at each spot where the game allows it, since a shared session counts twice at one location.
After each spot, check Progress > Collections > Exploration > Meditations and tick the spot here against the game's counter, not your memory.
Leave any spot that needs both characters together until after Chapter 2 unlocks playing as the pair, then return for it during the sweep.
The trophy unlocks when the counter reaches the full set of spots.
trophies.tip: One two-minute conversation in Chapter 1 is the difference between a relaxing sweep and a permanently open question — take the meditation when Lucia offers it, and let the other seventeen spots be the easy part.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; the count of 18 spots comes from the kit's starter data for this list. Possibly-missable Chapter 1 meditation, the both-characters counting rule and the tracking menu: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026; both sources note it is not yet confirmed whether the trophy requires that first meditation. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret's strand builds to this hunt, so the trophy sits inside his chain rather than in free roam: play his missions until the hunt is offered, then treat it as a tracking exercise — unique-animal hunts in this series are about following sign and choosing your moment, not about firepower. Go in with a full health bar, a suitable weapon for large game, and a vehicle you do not mind leaving at the trailhead.
steps: Advance Bret's strand until the unique-animal hunt opens.
Prepare before setting out: health, ammunition and a weapon suited to big game.
Track and take the animal as the hunt directs; the trophy unlocks on completion.
trophies.tip: If the trail goes cold, stop moving — sign is easier to read standing still than at a sprint, and spooking the animal costs more time than patience does.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete three full sets of collectible cards. Sets, not loose cards: a silver's worth of sweeping hides inside this wording, because three completed sets means finishing every card in each of three groups, including the awkward last card of each. Collect cards whenever the regional sweep passes them, but plan the endgame set by set — pick the set with the fewest cards missing, close it, then the next. Scattered collecting feels productive and finishes nothing.
steps: Pick up every card the regional sweeps put in reach, and note which sets they belong to.
When a set is within a few cards of done, detour and close it deliberately.
The silver unlocks when the third set is complete.
trophies.tip: The last card of a set is the whole job — budget your sweep time by sets missing one card, not by total cards found.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade and the count of 3 sets), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It at one hundred locations — and the verb is no longer a mystery, because both post-launch sources below describe the same mechanic. WAiNK is a phone app used for scanning: hold Up on the D-pad and then R1, and the objects in front of you that count are environmental points of interest, which the sources break down by kind — 31 Landmarks, 35 Curiosities and 23 Sculptures, plus the No Flusher tags — with more than one hundred available in total, so any one hundred of them completes the trophy and no single location is compulsory. GTABase adds that the app itself arrives automatically in Chapter 1. The method follows from the shape of the count: scanning is a two-button habit that costs seconds, so attach it to travel you already do — scan at every new viewpoint, building and oddity the story and the sweep put in front of you, rather than planning a scanning tour. And note the overlap the sources reveal: the same app, with the same two buttons, is how vehicles get scanned for Whip It Good and for Randy's Wish List, so one raised phone often feeds three cards at once.
steps: From Chapter 1, when the WAiNK app is on your phone, learn the gesture once: hold Up on the D-pad, then R1 to scan what you are looking at.
Scan every landmark, curiosity, sculpture and No Flusher tag the story and the regional sweep put in front of you; any 100 count, so never backtrack for one you passed.
When you stop to scan, sweep the phone across nearby vehicles too — the same scan feeds Whip It Good and checks cars against Randy's Wish List.
Check your running total in the game's progress menus whenever a region is finished, and top up in the densest district you know if a region left you short.
The silver unlocks at the hundredth scanned location.
trophies.tip: One hundred scans is a habit wearing a grind's clothes: players who scan at every stop finish without a tour, and players who plan a tour discover they needed a hundred separate stops.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade and the count of 100), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Scanning mechanic, input, location categories and Chapter 1 availability: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete fifty challenges. Challenges are the game's small-print objectives scattered through its activities and free roam, and fifty is a breadth count: the fastest route is to harvest the easy challenges attached to things you already do — driving, shooting, exploring — rather than hunting exotic ones. Check the challenge list whenever you finish a session and pick off anything sitting one step from done; those nearly-free completions are how fifty arrives without a dedicated grind.
steps: Open the challenges list early and skim what ordinary play already progresses.
After each session, finish any challenge that is one action away from complete.
The trophy unlocks at the fiftieth completed challenge.
trophies.tip: Breadth beats depth: fifty easy challenges finished is identical progress to fifty hard ones, so shop at the shallow end first.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade and the count of 50), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a four-star wanted level while your partner is with you, and get clear — off the watch list, because the window and the method are now confirmed by both post-launch sources below. The earliest you can attempt it is after Chapter 2's main mission Coffee Break, which unlocks free-roaming together as Jason and Lucia; from then on you call your partner by holding Right on the D-pad and pressing Triangle. Raise four stars with your partner present, then escape — and note the exact finish line both sources give: the trophy unlocks after you drive out of the red heat zone, not when you leave the flashing search area, so keep going until you are clear of the red. Their recommended route is specific: a fast sports motorcycle, and the train tunnel north of Ambrosia in Kelly County, where police have trouble following on the tracks and the helicopter cannot see you. If a helicopter is chasing, shoot at it until it breaks off. And if deliberate setups keep failing, both sources note the trophy tends to arrive on its own: the large bank vault robberies unlocked in Chapter 4 automatically give a four-star wanted level, and escaping one of those with your partner present is the same trophy earned by accident.
steps: Wait until Chapter 2's Coffee Break is complete, then call your partner (hold Right on the D-pad, press Triangle) so you are free-roaming together.
Raise your wanted level to four stars with your partner with you — sustained carnage gets there; a large bank vault robbery, once unlocked in Chapter 4, gives four stars automatically.
On a fast sports motorcycle, head for the train tunnel north of Ambrosia in Kelly County; ride the tracks through it to break police pursuit and helicopter sight.
Keep going until you have driven out of the red heat zone entirely — leaving only the flashing search area is not enough — and the trophy unlocks as you clear it.
trophies.tip: Most failed attempts end one zone too early: players relax when the flashing stops, inside the red. Ride until the red is behind you; the tunnel buys the distance, the zone boundary pays the trophy.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Unlock window (after Coffee Break), partner call input, heat-zone finish line, Ambrosia tunnel route and the bank-vault route: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in a row with your partner, without your wanted level dropping in between — off the watch list, because both post-launch sources below now give the working version of this run. It opens after Chapter 2's Coffee Break, when you can switch between and travel with both characters, and the targets are the robbery locations marked with green icons on the map. The level you must maintain is the red-and-blue flashing wanted level — PowerPyx is explicit that the red heat level is a different state and is not what this trophy tracks. Preparation is named, not implied: an armoured vest and sticky bombs from Ammu-Nation, and healing items (Zombix or Adrenaline, per PowerPyx), with your partner called in first (hold Right on the D-pad, press Triangle). The cluster both sources recommend is the three jewellery stores in the north of Vice City, available after Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs in Chapter 3; PowerPyx adds the detail that makes a robbery count — loot a couple of items in each store and ideally go into the back room and break the safe with sticky bombs, because leaving the first store before the police arrive can leave the run short, in which case a fourth store fixes it. Expect the unlock to lag: both sources report it can take about thirty seconds after the third shop, so do not restart a good run just because nothing popped at the till.
steps: After Chapter 2's Coffee Break, prepare: call your partner (hold Right on the D-pad, press Triangle), equip an armoured vest, and carry sticky bombs and a healing item.
Head for the three jewellery stores in the north of Vice City (available after Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs in Chapter 3) — the closest cluster of green-icon robbery targets.

Rob the first store properly: take a couple of items and, if you can, break the back-room safe with sticky bombs, then move to the second store while the red-and-blue flashing wanted level is still alive — never let it fully clear between stores.
Rob the second and third the same way, keeping the flashing wanted level continuous throughout.
Wait up to thirty seconds after leaving the third store for the delayed unlock; if it still has not landed, rob a fourth store while staying wanted and it should follow.
trophies.tip: The run fails in the gaps, not the stores: your wanted level is a baton, and the only rule of the relay is that it never touches the ground — if the flashing stops between shops, the count restarts, however good the robberies were.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Unlock window, flashing-level rule, preparation, north Vice City jewellery cluster, safe detail, delayed unlock and fourth-store fallback: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover one hundred different vehicles — and this card's method has been corrected, because discovery in this game is not what the series led us to expect. The old version told you to get in and drive each new model; both post-launch sources below say discovery is done by scanning, with the WAiNK app: hold Up on the D-pad to raise it, look at a vehicle and hold R1 to scan it into your database. Driving the vehicle is not required — GTABase is explicit that you do not need to drive them at all, and PowerPyx's fastest method is simply to stand beside a busy road and scan the traffic passing. That turns a hundred-vehicle grind into a posture: wherever you already are, when unfamiliar metal passes, scan it. Progress is visible under Touchpad > Progress > Vehicles, where scrolling each category shows its found total. Keep perspective, too: the 100% checklist wants 200 base-model vehicles scanned, so a player working that list passes this trophy's hundred on the way without a dedicated session.
steps: Learn the scan once: hold Up on the D-pad for the WAiNK app, look at a vehicle, hold R1 until it registers as discovered.
Scan unfamiliar vehicles wherever you meet them — parked rows in new districts, and passing traffic when you are standing anywhere busy.
For a deliberate push, stand beside a busy road and scan everything that passes until the session's new models dry up, then change district and repeat.
Check Touchpad > Progress > Vehicles to see the running total per category; the trophy unlocks at the hundredth distinct vehicle scanned.
trophies.tip: If your count stalls, the problem is your feet, not your garage: you are standing in districts whose traffic you have already scanned — move somewhere richer, portside or airborne, and the new models return.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade and the count of 100), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Scanning mechanic and inputs, no-driving rule, busy-road method and progress menu: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down five enemies inside one activation of Combat Focus, the game's slow-motion aiming state. Five in a single use means the attempt is about staging, not aim: you want a group of five or more enemies in one place, your focus meter full, and your targets prioritised before you trigger it. Gang locations and illegal operations are natural staging grounds. Line the shots up in order of threat, take them in one sweep, and do not waste the window repositioning.
steps: Find a spot with at least five enemies grouped together and your focus meter charged.
Plan your target order before activating — closest and most dangerous first.
Activate Combat Focus once and take down five before it ends.
trophies.tip: Set the stage at range with a weapon that kills in one hit per target; the window is long enough for five aimed shots, not five firefights.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade and the count of 5), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an 'unscheduled departure' at VCIA, the airport — off the watch list, because the joke now has a confirmed answer, and it is more specific than this card's original guess. Both post-launch sources below agree: the aircraft has to be one of the large passenger jets docked at a departure gate's boarding bridge; planes parked out on the airfield do not count. The easiest targets are the jets at gates E3 and E4 — GTABase's route is to drive through the airfield fence and use the door by the stairs next to the boarding bridge, while PowerPyx describes entering the plane, going upstairs to the cockpit, and backing it out to the airstrip. Either way the act is the same: steal the docked jet, take off, and fly about one kilometre away from the airport. Expect the unlock to lag the takeoff — PowerPyx puts the trigger distance at roughly 1 km (0.6 miles), so a departure that has not popped while you are still over the fence has not failed yet. The save-first habit from the old version of this card is still good practice for the drive in, but the experiment is over: this is a recipe now, not a theory.
steps: Save manually outside VCIA, then head for the passenger jets docked at departure gates E3 or E4 — not the planes parked on the open airfield.
Get in: drive through the airfield fence and use the door by the stairs next to the boarding bridge, or enter through the terminal on foot.
Go upstairs to the cockpit, back the jet out to the airstrip and take off.
Fly about 1 km away from the airport and give the delayed unlock a moment to land before judging the attempt.
trophies.tip: Docked is the whole word in this recipe: if the jet was sitting on the apron with no bridge attached, you stole the wrong plane beautifully — go back for one at a gate.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Docked-jet requirement, gates E3/E4, entry route and the roughly 1 km trigger distance: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is a pun and a warning: Rhinos are tanks, and it gets hot around them — off the watch list, because of the candidates this card originally listed (survive one, destroy one, ride in one, outrun one), the post-launch sources below confirm the third, with an address attached. Both PowerPyx and GTABase say the same thing: steal a tank from Mile Zero Air Station, on the south-west island in Mariana County, where the tanks stand at the south end of the base, and take out enemies from inside it until the trophy pops. PowerPyx's entry route is to drive through the gate, or take the stunt jump next to the south-east entrance. So the method inverts the old card's caution: you are not surviving an encounter with a Rhino, you are causing one, from the driver's seat, and the save you make beforehand is no longer for testing theories — it is for the drive home if the base visit goes wrong before the trophy lands. Keep shooting from inside the tank; getting out to fight on foot is the one version of this the sources do not describe.
steps: Save manually before travelling, then head to Mile Zero Air Station on the south-west island of Mariana County.
Enter the base — through the gate, or via the stunt jump by the south-east entrance — and go to the tanks at the south end.
Get into a tank and stay in it.
Take out enemies from inside the tank until the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tip: The trophy is a theft followed by a shooting spree, in that order and from that seat: if you are on foot admiring the Rhino, you are doing the old card's experiment, not this one's recipe.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Mile Zero Air Station location, tank position and the steal-and-shoot trigger: PowerPyx, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap, and GTABase, GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List, both checked 20 November 2026. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewellery store and stay undetected doing it. Detection is the fail state, so this robbery is a stealth exercise wearing a heist's clothes: case the store first — staff positions, sightlines, the exit you will actually use — and go at a quiet time with no weapon shown until you are sure you need one, if you need one at all. If you are spotted, do not finish the robbery out of stubbornness; walk away, let the heat die, and re-enter fresh, because a completed-but-detected robbery earns nothing here.
steps: Visit the jewellery store peacefully first and learn its layout and staff routine.
Enter quietly, take what the robbery allows without raising attention, and leave by your planned exit.
The trophy unlocks if the robbery completes with no detection.
trophies.tip: Plan this one before the loud robberies in the roadmap — stealth is a mindset, and it is easier to learn while you are not in a firefight habit.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape after each — the escape is in the official wording, so a vault emptied and a protagonist arrested is progress of zero. Five separate successful jobs are required. Build up to them: your first vault teaches you the timing of the response, so choose an easy one, stage a fast car facing the exit before you go in, and have a wanted-level plan (a route with cover, a vehicle swap, a quiet district to drain the stars in) rather than improvising at five stars.
steps: Scout a vault and stage your getaway car before entering.
Rob the vault, leave on your planned route, and lose the wanted level completely.
Repeat at four more vaults; the silver unlocks after the fifth clean escape.
trophies.tip: The robbery is the easy half — rehearse the escape route once without robbing anything, and the real run feels familiar.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade and the count of 5), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armoured truck and escape. One truck, one clean getaway. Armoured trucks are moving targets with a set route and a heavy response once breached, so the method is ambush, not chase: pick a quiet stretch of the truck's route, block it with a heavy vehicle of your own, breach it fast, and be gone on a pre-planned route before the response organises. Practise the breach once and accept the arrest if it teaches you the timing — the second attempt is the one that counts.
steps: Find an armoured truck's route and choose a quiet ambush point on it.
Block the truck, breach it and take the money quickly.
Escape on a planned route and lose the wanted level; the trophy unlocks on the clean getaway.
trophies.tip: Choose the ambush for its exits, not its drama — a dull junction with three ways out beats a cinematic bridge with none.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — fifty-two areas, per the starter data. Exploration registers by entering an area, so this trophy is a map-hygiene exercise: the regional sweep that collects your cards, spots and WAiNK locations will open most of the map on its own, and what remains at the end is usually a handful of small districts you drove through on a highway without ever technically entering. Finish by comparing your map against your sweep notes and visiting the gaps on purpose.
steps: Let the regional sweeps open the map as you collect everything else.
Near the end, scan the map for any area that never got a dedicated visit.
Enter each remaining area; the trophy unlocks when the fifty-second registers.
trophies.tip: Highways lie — passing through on a raised road may not count as visiting, so drop down into any district your count is missing.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; the count of 52 areas comes from the kit's starter data for this list. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each gang — nine gangs, per the starter data. The requirement is coverage, not volume: robbing the same gang nine times earns one-ninth of this trophy. Keep a written list of gangs hit, because operations look alike and memory is generous. Vary your approach as you go — by the fifth gang you will know the operation layouts well enough that the Gunslinger staging advice on this list becomes easy to set up inside them.
steps: Identify an illegal operation and which gang owns it before you go in.
Rob it, escape, and write the gang's name down.
Repeat until all nine gangs have been robbed once; the trophy unlocks on the ninth.
trophies.tip: Track gangs, not robberies — a notebook list of nine names is the difference between a method and a muddle.
trophies.source: Source: official PlayStation 5 trophy list (name, description, grade), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; the count of 9 gangs comes from the kit's starter data for this list. Method: this guide's own.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
